items.text: Survey: three events, records 305353 and 305355 missing, and no network (Event ID 3) events at all, so the export is partial
Process tree: cmd.exe with no arguments (no process-create event) → cmd /c (rec 305352) → desktopimgdownldr.exe (rec 305354), with svchost.exe kept separate rather than drawn as a child
Researched desktopimgdownldr.exe: a genuine Windows lock-screen image downloader that can be abused to fetch any URL, and noted the URL points at a .7z archive on an anonymous file host, not an image

Read the file event (rec 305356): svchost.exe, not the tool, wrote a new LockScreenImage_….7z in the user's Temp Personalization folder 1.4 s later, and explained it as a background download service (BITS) acting for the tool
Separated the observed links between file and command (path, .7z extension, timing, same profile) from the inferred ones (same contents), noting there's no hash or network event
Kept 'downloaded' separate from 'executed': nothing in the export shows the archive being opened, extracted or run
Tested the client's claim: no admin rights is supported (Medium integrity, user-profile path), but downloading and running from the user's profile need no admin, so it doesn't make the activity safe
Listed at least three things the logs can't tell you (e.g. the archive's contents and hash, the missing records, who typed the command, what happened next)
Classified it as a true positive, mapped it to T1105, and recommended collecting and analysing the archive before deciding on a wipe, plus isolating the workstation
